edges.description: Mycn gain of function is sufficient to produce postaxial polydactyly in the knock-in mouse. The limb mechanism between MYCN accumulation and extra digit formation has not been studied.

MYCN is the canonical neuroblastoma oncogene and Thr58Met recurs as a somatic mutation in neuroblastoma, so a germline stabilizing variant is a plausible predisposing lesion. The causal link is inferred from that oncogenic role and from two of three patients developing infantile neuroblastoma; it has not been tested experimentally in this syndrome.
Sustained cyclin D expression is the proposed driver of delayed cell-cycle exit and over-proliferation of cortical progenitors. This step is a hypothesis of the authors rather than a tested result.

nodes.description: The disease-causing missense variants (p.Thr58Met, p.Pro60Leu) sit in the N-terminal phosphodegron of MYCN. GSK3B phosphorylation of Thr58 marks MYCN for recognition by the FBXW7 ubiquitin ligase and proteasomal degradation. Both variants reduce Thr58 phosphorylation, so the mutant protein escapes FBXW7-mediated degradation.

nodes.description: Heterozygous knock-in of the patient Thr58Met variant. nodes.description: MYCN-T58M induced and prolonged expression of the G1 cyclins CCND1 and CCND2 in cultured neuronal progenitor and stem cells. CCND2 is itself the gene whose stabilizing variants cause megalencephaly-polymicrogyria-polydactyly-hydrocephalus syndrome 3, which shares megalencephaly and postaxial polydactyly with this disorder. The cyclin D link has been shown in vitro only; it was not measured in the knock-in mouse.
